subject: Procurement & hosting preference follow-up — Orion AI
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@orionai.com>, Leah Yu <leah@orionai.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Procurement & hosting preference follow-up — Orion AI

Hi Sanjay / Leah — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can get you a clean procurement path and pricing that maps to your purchasing rules.

Recap (from today's discovery)
- Primary use case: customer support augmentation (PHI redaction expected in some workflows).
- Expected initial footprint: 4–6 concurrent inference agents, ~2M tokens/month.
- Preference: predictable monthly spend for budgeting team; willingness to commit to a 12mo baseline if it lowers unit cost.
- Key constraints: procurement prefers PO for enterprise buys; tax/contract advantages if purchased via AWS Marketplace are possible but not required.

Questions / asks from procurement perspective
1) Preferred payment instrument: PO (Net 30) or corporate card? Can procurement@orionai.com accept a Marketplace contract?
2) Hosting model: do you need Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) or Private (VPC/on‑prem) for the PHI workloads, or would Hosted with a private tenancy suffice initially?
3) Commitment model: are you evaluating committed reserved capacity (12mo) vs on‑demand? If committed, can you share a target monthly commit (GPU-hours or $)?
4) Legal / SOW: will you need a quick SOW + DSAR/KMS language embedded (if so, point us to the procurement contact and any internal clause references).

Next steps I propose
- Please loop in procurement@orionai.com and share your procurement contact + preferred payment method.
- I’ll attach a short term sheet and a checklist for PO vs Marketplace flows.
- If you prefer, we can schedule a 30min procurement call next week with our commercial ops (Karthik) and solutions lead (Neha) to walk the PO paperwork and timeline.

Attached: short procurement checklist + term sheet (preview).

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
attachments: [Orion_Procurement_Form_2026.pdf (fillable), Redwood_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf (summary)]

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@orionai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Leah Yu <leah@orionai.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Procurement & hosting preference follow-up — Orion AI

Thanks Ben — useful recap. A few answers from our side and a short procurement form attached.

Answers:
- Procurement prefers PO / Net 30 for anything > $10k/month. For pilot <$10k we can pay by card. We generally prefer to avoid marketplace unless there's a specific tax/discount benefit — we can consider if you have a Marketplace listing that supports consolidated billing.
- PHI: Our security team wants data isolation. Ideally Dedicated or Private. For timeline reasons we may pilot on Hosted with strict tenancy and tokenized logs, then move to Dedicated if performance/cost prove out.
- Commit: Finance would like a 12mo committed baseline if it reduces overall cost and allows predictable budgeting — they asked for a modeled example (commit level vs unit price).
- Procurement contact is procurement@orionai.com (I’ve cc'd them here). Legal will need standard mutual NDA + a short SOW for pilot.

Attached form: "Orion_Procurement_Form_2026.pdf" — it has our PO template and billing contact.

Can we do a procurement/ops call Wed 12/9 10:00am PT?

— Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform Engineering
Orion AI
attachments: [Orion_Procurement_Form_2026.pdf]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 07 Dec 2026 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Procurement & hosting preference follow-up — Orion AI

Thanks Sanjay — looping procurement on this thread.

Procurement / Finance folks — quick notes to make the Wed 12/9 call productive:
- We can support PO / Net 30 for orders above your $10k threshold. For pilots under $10k we recommend card for speed.
- Marketplace consideration: Redwood is available on AWS Marketplace (metered + 1yr SaaS options). Marketplace can simplify tax and consolidated billing but adds a procurement catalog step; if you require consolidated AWS billing it can be a clean path.
- Hosting/segregation options: 1) Hosted with private tenancy + KMS & token-level log controls (fastest), 2) Dedicated pool (predictable latency & data isolation), 3) Private (VPC or on‑prem) for regulated PHI — estimated lead times: Hosted (immediate), Dedicated (4–6 weeks for capacity provisioning), Private (6–12 weeks depending on onboarding).
- Commitment tiers: we can model 12mo commit discounts against list; typical commit breakpoints are $50k/mo, $100k/mo (we'll provide modeled unit economics).

Neha / Karthik — can you prepare a 1‑page commit vs on‑demand cost comparison for the 2M token/month profile + estimate of Dedicated SKU (4–6 agents) before the Wed call? Also include a brief note on compliance controls we can surface for the PO. I’ll share the procurement form with you both.

Proposed calendar invite: Wed 9 Dec (12/9) 10:00–10:30 PT — procurement@orionai.com, Sanjay, Leah, Neha, Karthik, Ben.

Ben
attachments: [Redwood_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf]

Ben / Karthik — quick internal note after reading Sanjay's answers.

Action items I will own before Wed call:
- Build two pricing scenarios (12mo commit vs on‑demand) for 2M tokens/mo and for Dedicated 4‑agent pool. Include blended per-token cost, estimated GPU-hours, and expected monthly invoice shape.
- Draft a short compliance summary: KMS integration, log redaction controls, and SOC2 evidence pointers.
- Prepare a one‑pager for marketplace pros/cons (billing consolidation vs onboarding friction).

Open Qs for commercial ops (Karthik):
- Do we have a published commit breakpoints doc I can reference for discounts? (if not, I’ll use conservative estimates and flag as preliminary)
- For PO processing: standard Net 30 vs Net 45 options — do we offer Net 45 for enterprise finance exceptions?

I’ll have materials into the HubSpot deal record and Drive by EOD Thursday.

Neha
